consumer_summary.what_it_is: β-Selinene is a naturally occurring sesquiterpene, a type of aromatic molecule that helps give certain plants their distinct, earthy, and woody scents. As a volatile organic compound, it readily evaporates into the air, making it a key player in the fragrance and flavor profiles of the botanicals that produce it. You most likely encounter it in the crisp scent of fresh celery or the complex aroma of a hoppy beer.
consumer_summary.found_in: This molecule is notably found in Apium graveolens (celery) and Humulus lupulus (hops), contributing to their characteristic aromas. It is also present in a wide variety of other aromatic plants, including Artemisia annua (sweet wormwood) and Leptospermum scoparium (manuka).
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to β-selinene for its prominent role in plant defense systems, particularly its ability to ward off fungal pathogens and insects. This natural protective quality has sparked interest in its potential applications as an antimicrobial and antioxidant agent in human health and agriculture. The strongest evidence exploring these effects comes from human observational studies (Oxford level 2b), which are mapping out how β-selinene-rich extracts interact with microbes and oxidative stress.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether β-selinene can influence cancer cell growth or survival, given its presence in traditionally used medicinal plants.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, double-blind clinical trial in humans evaluating the effects of a standardized β-selinene supplement alongside standard care, measuring tumor markers and quality of life over six months.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Early animal work points toward a potential calming effect, raising the question of whether this terpene contributes to the relaxing properties of hops and other botanicals.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, placebo-controlled human trial measuring self-reported anxiety scores and salivary cortisol levels after inhalation of isolated β-selinene over a four-week period.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Scientists are investigating if β-selinene could be harnessed as a natural anti-infective agent to combat resistant bacterial and fungal strains.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized controlled trial testing a topical β-selinene formulation against a placebo for the treatment of mild superficial fungal infections over four weeks.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: If this bears out, β-selinene could serve as a natural, plant-derived alternative to synthetic insect repellents like DEET.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A human field trial comparing the mosquito-landing rates on skin treated with a β-selinene lotion versus a standard DEET repellent over an 8-hour exposure period.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far is human observational work (Oxford 2b); most of the rest is animal and lab research focusing on its antimicrobial and antioxidant properties.
